ov: Narrow-waisted insects that are neither bees nor ants, with tens of thousands of species. Yellowjackets and hornets live in colonies with a queen, but most wasp species live alone.

why.dg: Many wasps can sting, and colonies defend their nests. People are stung most in late summer, when workers look for sugary food.

df: Many are predators or parasites of other insects; some feed on nectar.

cf.tip: Bees evolved from wasps. Bees feed on nectar and pollen and have feathery hairs for carrying pollen; most wasps hunt.

fx: Wasps control crop pests such as whitefly in tomato greenhouses.
notes: Group entry. The existing fact (invented paper by chewing wood) is confirmed: social wasps build nests from wood fibres softened by chewing.
